value.title: PR freeze check before verdicts (F92)
value.summary: `just pr-freeze <pr>` verifies a PR head is final (remote and gh agree, main base, CLEAN, CI passed, ready, migration numbered above main, Delivers parses) before verdicts are requested or READY is sent.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Verdicts are only worth something at a final head. Tonight the PM checked finality by hand, and got it wrong once. This plan encodes the check as one read-only command. One coder (tapir).

sections.name: goals
value: `just pr-freeze <pr>` verifies a PR head is final (remote and gh agree, main base, CLEAN, CI passed, ready, migration numbered above main, Delivers parses) before verdicts are requested or READY is sent.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Any daemon or CI-gate change; this is a hand-run harness tool.

value.claim: One command says whether a PR head is final for verdicts. `just pr-freeze <pr>` (a script under harness/scripts with a just recipe; read-only; gh and git only) prints, for the PR: the head from `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<n>/head` and from `gh pr view`, and whether they agree; the base branch and whether it is main; mergeStateStatus (CLEAN, DIRTY, BEHIND, UNSTABLE) with the reason; each CI check's latest run by name (an older failed run superseded by a newer pass counts as pass, an in-progress one as not final); draft or ready; and whether a review worktree exists at exactly that head (`git worktree list` for a path ending in -<pr>-<head7>, at that commit). It exits 0 and says FINAL only when the two heads agree, the base is main, the state is CLEAN, every check's latest run passed, and the PR is not draft; otherwise it exits non-zero naming each failing condition and the next step (merge main, wait for CI, mark ready).

Tonight's other freeze lessons are checked too. It reports each migration the PR adds (crates/store/migrations) against main's highest and SCHEMA_VERSION on both sides, and flags a number not above main's highest (the merge-order rule, 07 Nov). It parses the PR body's Delivers: line with the same parser CI uses and flags prose or a missing line. With --worktree it creates the detached review worktree at the verified head if none exists and prints its path.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). No daemon change. Run by hand, once per verdict request: one ls-remote, two or three gh calls, a few local git reads. No loop, timer or poll.

Docs and states. The pij skill's PM and verdict sections say to run `just pr-freeze <pr>` before requesting verdicts and before sending READY; AGENTS.md's harness tooling list names it; docs/difficulties.md marks F92 resolved. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: F92 (offered by reviewer pij-double-bobcat, 07 Nov): on 07 Nov, #149's head moved four times under review (642e64b, a63edce, fb87062, a force-push that landed for a minute) and pm-001 repointed seats on a coder's report of a push that hadn't stuck; #136, #148 and #150 went DIRTY after merges and #152's migration order was mis-stated. Each was caught by hand with ls-remote, gh pr view and CI reads. The merge-order migration rule and the Delivers check (plan 209) already exist; this puts them in front of the verdict request.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
